title: 2 Chronicles 35
paragraphs: ¹ Josiah celebrated a Passover to the LORD in Jerusalem, and the Passover lamb was slaughtered on the fourteenth day of the first month. ² He appointed the priests to their duties and encouraged them in the service of the LORD's house. ³ He said to the Levites, who instructed all of Israel and who were consecrated to the LORD: "Put the sacred ark in the temple that Solomon son of David, king of Israel, built. You do not need to carry it on your shoulders any longer. Now serve the LORD your God and his people Israel. ⁴ Organize yourselves by family groups according to your divisions, as prescribed by David king of Israel and by his son Solomon. ⁵ Take your positions in the sanctuary according to the family divisions of your fellow countrymen, the laypeople, and according to the divisions of the Levites."

⁶ "Slaughter the Passover lambs, consecrate yourselves, and prepare the offerings for your fellow Israelites, doing everything in accordance with the word of the LORD through Moses." ⁷ Josiah donated thirty thousand lambs and young goats and three thousand bulls from his own possessions to the people — all for the Passover offerings for everyone present. ⁸ His officials also made freewill offerings to the people, the priests, and the Levites. Hilkiah, Zechariah, and Jehiel, the administrators of God's house, contributed two thousand six hundred Passover offerings and three hundred bulls to the priests. ⁹ Conaniah, along with his brothers Shemaiah and Nethanel, and Hashabiah, Jeiel, and Jozabad, the chief Levites, donated five thousand Passover offerings and five hundred bulls to the Levites. ¹⁰ When everything was organized, the priests stood at their places and the Levites in their divisions, as the king had commanded.

¹¹ They slaughtered the Passover lambs, and the priests sprinkled the blood handed to them while the Levites skinned the animals. ¹² They set aside the burnt offerings for the family groups of the people, to offer to the LORD as prescribed in the Book of Moses. They did the same with the bulls. ¹³ They roasted the Passover animals over the fire as prescribed, and boiled the other holy offerings in pots, caldrons, and pans, then quickly distributed portions to all the people. ¹⁴ After that, they prepared portions for themselves and for the priests — the Aaronic priests were busy offering the burnt offerings and the fat portions until nightfall, so the Levites prepared portions for themselves and for the Aaronic priests. ¹⁵ The musicians, the descendants of Asaph, were at their posts as commanded by David, Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun the king's seer. The gatekeepers stood at every gate; they did not have to leave their posts, for their fellow Levites prepared portions for them.

¹⁶ So all the service of the LORD was set in order that day to celebrate the Passover and offer burnt offerings on the altar of the LORD, as King Josiah had commanded. ¹⁷ The Israelites who were present celebrated the Passover at that time and kept the Festival of Unleavened Bread for seven days. ¹⁸ No Passover like this had been kept in Israel since the days of the prophet Samuel — none of the kings of Israel had ever kept a Passover like the one Josiah kept with the priests, the Levites, all of Judah and Israel who were present, and the people of Jerusalem. ¹⁹ This Passover was kept in the eighteenth year of Josiah's reign. ²⁰ After all this, when Josiah had set the temple in order, Necho king of Egypt marched up to fight at Carchemish on the Euphrates, and Josiah went out to confront him.

²¹ But Necho sent envoys to him with this message: "What quarrel is there between us, king of Judah? I am not attacking you today but the nation at war with me. God has told me to hurry — stop interfering with God, who is with me, or he will destroy you." ²² Josiah, however, would not turn away from him; he disguised himself in order to fight, refusing to listen to Necho's message from the mouth of God. He went to fight in the Valley of Megiddo. ²³ Archers shot King Josiah, and he told his officers, "Take me away — I am badly wounded." ²⁴ So his servants lifted him out of his chariot and carried him in a second chariot to Jerusalem, where he died and was buried in the tombs of his ancestors. All of Judah and Jerusalem mourned for Josiah. ²⁵ Jeremiah composed laments for Josiah, and all the male and female singers still recall him in their laments to this day. These laments became a tradition in Israel and are recorded in the Laments.

²⁶ The rest of the acts of Josiah, and his acts of faithful devotion in keeping with what is written in the law of the LORD, ²⁷ and his deeds from beginning to end — all are recorded in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah.
